extracted.intended_audience: Researchers/authors submitting manuscripts to PLOS ONE
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and requirements authors must satisfy for a manuscript to be considered for publication in PLOS ONE, covering scope, originality, technical standards, ethics, reporting, and data availability. Intended to guide manuscript preparation and editorial/peer-review decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: 1. The study presents the results of original research.
rubrics_metrics.description: PLOS ONE is designed to communicate original research. We welcome submissions in the natural sciences, medical research, engineering, as well as the related social sciences and humanities that will contribute to the base of academic knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly excludes: reviews, case reports, study protocols (except Registered Report evaluation framework), hypothesis/proposal papers, letters/commentaries/essays, opinion pieces, policy papers, clinical practice guidelines, any other type of secondary literature, monographs. Occasionally commissioned Collection Reviews/Overviews only for solicited Collections. Accepted/considered article types (with conditions): Registered Reports (protocols and outcome reports), systematic reviews (methods ensuring comprehensive/unbiased sampling), submissions describing methods/software/databases/tools (must follow reporting guidelines), qualitative research (only if adheres to study design and reporting guidelines), and studies reporting negative/null results. Authors should consult submission guidelines for discipline-specific additional requirements (e.g., systematic review methods, reporting standards).

rubrics_metrics.name: 2. Results reported have not been published elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.description: PLOS ONE does not accept for publication studies that have already been published, in whole or in part, elsewhere in the peer-reviewed literature. All figures included in manuscripts should be original, and should not have been published in any previous publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manuscripts currently under consideration elsewhere will not be accepted. Preprints (e.g., bioRxiv, arXiv), theses, or conference presentations do not preclude consideration. Authors must not submit work already published in peer-reviewed literature. For replication studies or submissions similar to previous work, authors must provide a sound scientific rationale and clearly reference and discuss existing literature; derivative or un-justified replications will likely be rejected. See guidance on posting preprints and related submission procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: 3. Experiments, statistics, and other analyses are performed to a high technical standard and are described in sufficient detail.
rubrics_metrics.description: Experiments must have been conducted rigorously, with appropriate controls and replication. Sample sizes must be large enough to produce robust results, where applicable. Methods and reagents must be described in sufficient detail for another researcher to reproduce the experiments described.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expectations include appropriate experimental design, adequate controls, replication, appropriate sample size and statistical power where applicable, and thorough methodological detail (including reagents) enabling reproducibility. Failure to meet technical rigor or to provide sufficient methodological detail may lead to rejection. Follow discipline-specific reporting guidelines (see submission guidelines) for methodological reporting standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: 4. Conclusions are presented in an appropriate fashion and are supported by the data.
rubrics_metrics.description: The data presented in the manuscript must support the conclusions drawn. Submissions will be rejected if the interpretation of results is unjustified or inappropriate, so authors should avoid overstating their conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors may discuss possible implications, but these should be clearly identified as hypotheses rather than definitive conclusions. Avoid over-interpretation and ensure claims are proportional to the evidence. Peer review and editorial assessment will evaluate whether conclusions are justified by the presented results.

rubrics_metrics.name: 5. The article is presented in an intelligible fashion and is written in standard English.
rubrics_metrics.description: PLOS ONE does not copyedit accepted manuscripts, so the language in submitted articles must be clear, correct, and unambiguous. We may reject papers that do not meet these standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If language is difficult to understand or includes many errors, editors may recommend independent editorial help before revision. Authors are advised to use scientific editing/manuscript editing services if needed. Clear presentation includes organization, clarity of argument, and unambiguous writing in standard English.

rubrics_metrics.name: 6. The research meets all applicable standards for the ethics of experimentation and research integrity.
rubrics_metrics.description: Research published in PLOS ONE must have been conducted to the highest ethical standards. We reserve the right to reject any submission that does not meet these standards, which in some cases are more stringent than local ethical standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approval from the relevant body is required for studies involving: humans (live or tissue), including observational or survey-based studies or those with personal data; animals (live or tissue), including observational studies; cell lines that are not commercially available; field sampling; and work with potential biosafety implications. If approval was not obtained, authors must explain why it was not required. Publication ethics expectations: PLOS ONE is a member of COPE and expects compliance with best practices on authorship, dual publication, plagiarism, figure manipulation, and competing interests. Concerns should be addressed to the editorial office. Contact plosone@plos.org for compliance questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: 7. The article adheres to appropriate reporting guidelines and community standards for data availability.
rubrics_metrics.description: Results must be rigorously reported, as appropriate based on community standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must follow discipline-specific reporting guidelines (see submission guidelines). Data availability: authors must follow standards/practices for depositing data in publicly available resources (e.g., gene sequences, microarray data, structural studies). Failure to comply with community data deposition standards may result in rejection. See PLOS ONE data availability policy for details on acceptable data sharing and deposition practices.
